'''Olga Beaver''' (12 November 1942 – 7 December 2012<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|date=May 2013|title=Deaths of AMS members|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201305/201305-full-issue.pdf|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|volume=60|issue=5 |pages=626|access-date=2 May 2021}}</ref>), informally called '''Ollie''',<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=9 December 2012|title=Olga Beaver Obituary (1942 - 2012) - Pittsfield, MA - The Berkshire Eagle|url=https://www.legacy.com/amp/obituaries/berkshire/161551827|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427102131/https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/berkshire/obituary.aspx?pid=161551827|archive-date=27 April 2017|access-date=2 May 2021|website=www.legacy.com|language=en}}</ref> was a [[Czech-American]] [[mathematician]] and Professor of Mathematics at [[Williams College]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://math.williams.edu/professor-beavers-memorial-minute/|title=Professor Beaver's Memorial Minute|work=Mathematics & Statistics|access-date=2017-04-26|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2" />  She was the recipient of the second [[Louise Hay Award]] from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/hay-award/hay-award-1992/|title=Louise Hay Award 1992 Winner: Olga Beaver|website=awm-math.org|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref>  She is noted for having founded the Summer Science Program at Williams. She served as the director of the SSP for many years, and was the chair of the Mathematics Department at Williams for five and a half years.<ref name=":0" />

== Early life ==
Beaver was born in [[Prague, Czechoslovakia]] to Ing. Achill Jozef Roziňák and Zora Marie (Lisa) Roziňáková on 12 November 1942.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=The Passing of Olga R. Beaver|url=https://president.williams.edu/writings-and-remarks/in-memoriam/the-passing-of-olga-r-beaver/|access-date=2021-05-02|website=Office of the President|language=en-US}}</ref> Her earliest memory was of hiding in her apartment basement during a [[bombing raid]].<ref name=":0" /> After attending schools in Prague, she fled with her family at night to [[West Germany]] in 1949.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /> She lived in [[Refugee camp|refugee camps]] in [[Munich]], and then in [[London]] for two years and nine months, where she witnessed the [[coronation of Elizabeth II]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" /> She to the [[United States]] in 1952 and spent the rest of her childhood in [[Long Island]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" /> or their family came only in 1957, when they are documented in the Ellis Island list of immigrants<ref>[https://www.myheritage.cz/research/category-4000/p%C5%99ist%C4%9Bhovalectvi-cestovani?action=query&formId=immigration&formMode=1&qname=Name+fn.Achill+fnmo.1+ln.Rozi%C5%88%C3%A1k+lnmo.3&qevents-event0=Event+et.any+epmo.similar&qevents=List&useTranslation=1&tr_ad_group=300x250+Records+Carousel+Billiongraves&tr_camp_id=9672840&tr_device=c&tr_campaign_id=%EBuy&tr_creative=recordscarousel&tr_country=ct%3DCZ&st=&city=29200&dma=0&zp=160+00&bw=4&tr_funnel=SuperSearch&tr_placement=Billiongraves&tr_ifid=Billiongraves_250388634&partner_name=billiongraves&dclid=CP-i-4KA0vYCFV6Ggwcdn7ABlg My Heritage. Achille and Olga Rozinak]</ref> 

== Education ==
Beaver began her undergraduate education at [[Smith College]]; while still enrolled, she married Donald deBlasiis (Don) Beaver. She left the college in 1962 when she became pregnant.<ref name=":0" />  She began taking classes at Southern Connecticut State College. After her husband finished his Ph.D. in 1966, the family moved to [[Kansas City, Missouri|Kansas City]], [[Missouri]], where Olga continued her work on her bachelor's degree at the [[University of Missouri–Kansas City]], completing her bachelor's in 1968 and her master's in 1969 (also at  UMKC).<ref name=":0" /> She was a mathematics professor at Williams College from 1 July 1971 until her death.<ref name=":3" /> In 1972, Beaver enrolled in the Ph.D. program at [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].<ref name=":0" /> She earned her doctorate from UMass in 1979, in the mathematics of quantum logic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=47353|title=Olga Beaver - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2017-04-26}}</ref> She pursued research in [[measure theory]] and [[probability theory]].<ref name=":4" />

Beaver died of [[Stage 4 cancer|stage 4 metastatic breast cancer]] on 7 December 2012 at her home, having been diagnosed with [[breast cancer]] in September 2009.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /> However, she continued teaching until 9 November 2012.<ref name=":0" /> At the time of her death, she had been a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for 36 years.<ref name=":2" />

== Personal life ==
Beaver enjoyed [[teaching]] mathematics, [[cooking]], [[gardening]], [[reading]], and [[interior design]].<ref name=":3" /> She traveled to Prague biannually since 1992, and was pleased to have her [[Czech citizenship]] reinstated.<ref name=":3" /> She had two children and five grandchildren.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" />

== Awards and honors ==
Beaver was honored with the 2nd Louise Hay Award in 1992.<ref name=":1" />
